### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `eea9af5be5a05c06869e4192aa3d40b4c0f2686d` — the merge of head `1e9d5ba927d855691cfadd9704a2dea96756c9f3` into base `b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin eea9af5be5a05c06869e4192aa3d40b4c0f2686d && git checkout eea9af5be5a05c06869e4192aa3d40b4c0f2686d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20 1e9d5ba927d855691cfadd9704a2dea96756c9f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20 && git merge --no-ff 1e9d5ba927d855691cfadd9704a2dea96756c9f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b62260cb819a2fba6fb0c44ee9b4a0a4e53b3b20` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40693a3456322fe182c67a2022612a4b190d82da`
Local-runs: none

Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-10T22:09Z (conclusions are the gate verdicts). Required seven: `Lint & Repo Gates` success · `TypeScript Type Check` success (source gates, workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates all success) · `Build Core` success · `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` success · `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success · `Dogfood Regression Gate` 2/3 and 3/3 success, 1/3 in_progress · `Test Core` **2/6 FAILURE**, 1/6 3/6 4/6 5/6 6/6 in_progress. Advisory: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs, No other open PR (issue / single-writer path), Part-of, card-claims-branch all success; Console Pin Gate and Packed-tarball skipped.

### ① Derived judgments

Diff: 28 files, +711/−59, merge-base `a360cee92e` = the PR base; equals the PR file list byte for byte.

- **The widening.** `FieldSchema.returnType` gains `currency`: an enum member, no key — `authorable-surface` rows are keys (`data/Field:returnType`), `json-schema.manifest/` is a name roster, `api-surface/` and `export-origins/` are spec-export rosters and spec adds no export — right, nothing owed; `Type Check · source gates` (runs `check:generated --reconcile-only` and `check:docs`) is green on this head.
- **Readers, census at head** (`git grep returnType` over `packages/**`, non-test): `FORMULA_RETURN_TYPE_AS_FIELD_TYPE` gains an explicit `currency → currency` row and the text, number and boolean doors all read that map (`filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts:290`, `filter-number-comparand-declared-type.ts:445`, `filter-boolean-comparand-declared-type.ts:318`): judged as the `currency` FieldType — text operator refused, number door judged (`currency` is in `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES`), boolean door not-judged — explicit arms, each pinned — right. `display-name.ts:126` tests `rt === 'text'` positively; currency is not title-eligible by that test, not a default arm, and ADR-0079 (the only ADR naming `returnType`) is text-only — unchanged by design, right. `aggregate-field-type-compatibility.ts` refuses `formula` by type and never reads `returnType` — unchanged by design, right. `service-analytics` `measure-result-type.ts` is a two-argument rule with no `returnType` read and `native-sql-strategy.ts` reads none; the walk test now reads the five members off the schema and holds `currency` to `undefined` — right. `ui/component.zod.ts:7201` takes `FieldSchema.shape.returnType` by reference; describe text only — right. objectql `text/number/boolean-*-door.ts`, plugin-security `rls-compiler.ts:515/543` and `security-plugin.ts:10357` relay the string into the spec verdicts with no table of their own — right. `metadata-core` fls `returnType: keep`, driver-sql `returnType: 'storage'`, lint message strings and the `returnType: 'text'` system-object declarations are key-level or literal, not member readers — right. The boolean door's fixture type (`'boolean' | 'text'`, :503) is a two-row fixture by design; the text and number fixtures now derive from `Field['returnType']` — right.
- **`currencyConfig` on a formula.** At the merge-base `FieldSchema`'s superRefine type-gates `maxLength`, `minLength`, `valueDomain`, `rows`, `dueLike`, `options`, `multiple`, `reference` only; `currencyConfig` is a plain optional (`field.zod.ts:1775`) — "already admitted, unread" holds. Absent on a currency formula means `dynamic` (the tenant default currency), the same as on a currency field: `CurrencyConfigSchema` defaults `currencyMode: 'dynamic'` and its describes say `dynamic` displays the tenant default; `formula-currency-result.test.ts` holds a formula's parse output and refusals equal to a currency field's over four configs and three malformed ones — consistent, right. Docblocks and describes now name both readers — right.
- **`inferFormulaReturn`.** Exported from `@objectstack/formula`'s single `.` entry via `index.ts`, with `FormulaReturnDeclaration` and `FormulaSourceField` — a published surface; the package has no api-surface or export-origins snapshot, so nothing to regenerate. It stamps `currency` only when `inferCelType` (over the ternary-rewritten source) answers int/uint/double/dyn AND the dimensional walk proves one amount; every other case returns `inferExpressionType(input, { fields })` verbatim, and `inferCelType(src, [])` is the default-parameter spelling of `inferCelType(src)`, so the no-fields answer is identical (`InferredValueType` is the four members plus `unknown`, which maps to `{}`) — as claimed and pinned. Two fixed source currencies combined (`record.amount + record.fee_eur`, USD with EUR): `join` answers unproven, falls through, stamps `{ returnType: 'number' }` with no `currencyConfig` — pinned at `formula-return.test.ts:295-297` beside fixed-with-dynamic and the ternary form; a plain `number`, never a currency it cannot name — right. Minor, consistent: a fixed source declaring no `defaultCurrency` stamps `CNY`, the schema default a currency field itself displays.
- **Generated artifacts.** `en.metadata-forms.generated.ts`: its two moved leaves equal the two `field.form.ts` helpText sources verbatim (the header: en is rewritten from source); option labels are not extracted (no `Boolean` leaf exists), so the new `Currency` option adds no key — right. zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES: the same two leaves re-translated by hand, keys unchanged — the header's own rule for a changed source — right. `content/docs/references/**` (field, object twice, migration twice, component): equal to the new describes, `check:docs` green on the head — right.
- **`object.form.ts`.** The edit is the comment plus one `{ label: 'Currency', value: 'currency' }` option (4+/1−), nothing else. `form-return-type-options.test.ts` holds `FORMS` = objectForm + fieldForm to "offers exactly the members FieldSchema declares — no more, no fewer", so the row had to move with the enum — required. #22713 merged 20:27Z before the edit, and no other open PR (all 12 scanned, every page) touches `object.form.ts`, `field.zod.ts` or formula `src/**` — right.
- **Prose.** `field-types.mdx`, `formulas.mdx`, `validation-rules.mdx` state the declaration, where its currency lives and the authoring producer; no sentence says a currency formula renders as money today; no stale four-member list survives in any hand-written tree. `formulas.mdx` Financial Calculations still declare `number` — acknowledged in the PR, carried. Right.
- **Carried item, not a defect of this diff.** `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:253` "(no 'currency')" is outside the diff (restored at the head to the merge-base blob) and goes false when this lands; the seat carries it to the skills lane.
- ⛔ **WRONG — a required gate is red and this diff made it so.** The `field.form.ts` `visibleWhen` widening (`data.type == 'currency' || (data.type == 'formula' && data.returnType == 'currency')`) adds two `==` literal comparisons to the shipped `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY` corpus, and `packages/lint/src/validate-predicate-path-refs.test.ts:774` pins that corpus count at 62 with a per-predicate ledger in its comment. `Test Core (2/6)` reads 64 and fails (`Failed: @objectstack/lint#test`, 1 failed / 6317 passed; the three other ELIFECYCLE lines are turbo cancellations, the summary names lint alone). The same shard is green on `main` at `a360cee92e` and `0f77ff5202`, so the red is this diff's, and `Test Core` is a required context. The dev's package set (spec, formula, objectql, service-analytics, platform-objects) never ran `@objectstack/lint`. Fix in the same PR: move the pin to 64 and add its ledger line naming `field :: currencyConfig` (`data.type == 'formula'`, `data.returnType == 'currency'`), or write the gate as an `in`-list the rule does not count; then re-measure the shard.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22727-formula-currency-result.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor` (enum widening, describes) — right; `@objectstack/formula: minor` (new export) — right; `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch` (help-text leaves only) — right; `service-analytics` moved a test only and `objectql` is untouched, so both correctly absent; not `skip-changeset`.
- Clause-②: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and in the changeset body — the arm matches an accept-set widening; `check-changeset-no-major`'s `yes` floor is PR-scoped and refuses only when every moved package is `patch` (two are `minor`) — clean; lockstep bumps platform-objects with them.
- ADR-0087: `check-adr-0087-registration` judges declared-breaking changesets only and says in its own text that a widening adds no signal and is not a break — no disposition marker and no registry entry owed; `Check Changeset` success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round 1, deviation 1 (`object.form.ts` edited after #22713 merged; other open PRs not re-scanned): measured above — none touches it — answered, accepted.
- Round 1, deviation 2 (files beyond `packages/spec`): formula is the claim's "plus `@objectstack/formula` if touched"; the analytics test is a reader's pin the claim names; `ui/component.zod.ts` is in `packages/spec/src/**`; the translation bundles are named; hand docs are ordinary; the skills line was reverted in round 2 — inside the surface, answered.
- Round 1, deviation 3 (attribution): the head commit ends with `Claude-Session:` and `Co-authored-by: Claude` (the model-free pair AGENTS.md prescribes); the PR body carries no footer after the PATCH, durable attribution lives in the commits — acceptable.
- Round 1, deviation 4 (`(#22727)` in a WIP subject): squash rewrites it; the trailer gate is green — accepted.
- Round 2 (body corrected in three places; footer omitted on edit; Tests/Gates cite `20d64a3102`/`de9f741f33`): the body names no skills edit and the file list holds no `skills/**` (Governed Surface Queue Guard success); the head differs from `de9f741f33` by the one restored skills file (1+/1−), so the cited readings stand for this code — except that the lint shard was never in them, which ① names.
- open_questions: both reports `[]` — none to answer.
- Out-of-scope carriers in the reports (objectui stamp and renderer, MCP `validate_expression`, the Financial Calculations examples, admitted-and-unread `currencyConfig` on a non-currency formula): noted in the PR; nothing escalated — the objectui half is the card's own named follow-up.
